decision: Before the first dispatch the controller commits its own edits in the shared worktree (or gives writers another worktree) and, for a vendored upstream or a markdown-forbidding plan, turns the reformat-md-tables hook off and checks git status after the first dispatch.

anchors: Never end your turn to wait for it: nothing wakes you
put them in the gate.py command as its suite
decision: The implementer template runs the full suite through gate.py and, when the call is moved to the background, reads the named output file in short calls until the closing line; its Committing section forbids amend, rebase, add -A and stash in a shared worktree and makes a gate refusal over an untouched file a verbatim BLOCKED report. A fix dispatch copies both parts, with the covering tests as its gate suite.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for gate.py, rebase, background in the template. GREEN opus and haiku ran the suite through gate.py, polled the output, refused to amend, reported BLOCKED verbatim, and kept the focused test outside gate.py; the full-suite vs one-line-fix contradiction both reported was closed and re-probed.

reopen_if: Writers following the template still idle on a backgrounded gate, or a shared-worktree commit is rewritten by another writer.
why: A redirect-plus-echo-RC gate form is refused by block-masked-gate-exit once the harness backgrounds the call; writers idled waiting on their own background run; a fixer's amend rewrote a parallel writer's commit.

anchors: does the fix change behaviour a release already ships?
Stop the run UNFINISHED: dispatch neither the fix nor the next task
Dispatch the fix as a commit of its own, apart from the task's plan-conforming work
treat it as shipped and stop
decision: In a headless run, a finding whose fix changes what the plan text requires is routed by whether the fix changes behaviour a release already ships: if it does (or you cannot tell), the run stops UNFINISHED with the question in EXECUTION-USER-REVIEW.md and a final message beginning UNFINISHED:; if it does not, the fix goes in as its own revertible commit, is logged with a reopen-if line, and the run continues. A run with a human present still asks.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-08 (Split by released behaviour); RED probes on the old text continued past a released-behaviour finding with a success-reading message, and kept the plan reading of an unreleased one

reopen_if: the harness gains a way to pause a headless run for an answer and resume it, or a measured run shows the released/unreleased judgement going wrong often enough to cost more than stopping
why: A question that ends a headless turn reads as the run finishing: a controller asked one after 3 of 14 tasks and the run exited as a success. Stopping on every such finding kills long runs over small conflicts; continuing on every one ships a wrong guess about released behaviour.

decision: Rejected: in a headless run, always log a plan-text finding and continue with the reversible reading.
